author: Triage Nurse
note_text:
Sudden onset severe R leg pain. Pt alert, oriented, visibly distressed.

Exam:
- R limb pale, cool to touch

Obs:
- BP 150/85
- HR 110 (irregular)
- RR 18
- Temp 36.8
- SpO₂ 97% RA

Impression: urgent vascular emergency suspected. Pt prioritized for MD review.

author: ED Physician
note_text:
84M w/ acute R lower limb pain started ~2h prior. Associated numbness + weakness. No trauma.
PMH: AF (no anticoag), HTN, HLD

Exam:
CV: irregularly irregular pulse
RLL:
- pale, cold
- absent distal pulses
- delayed cap refill
- ↓ sensation
- motor weakness

Assessment: acute limb ischemia, likely embolic (AF-related).
Plan:
- IV heparin
- analgesia
- urgent CTA
- vascular referral

author: ED Nurse
note_text:
IV access secured. Heparin infusion commenced.
Pain 8/10 → IV morphine given, good effect.
R leg remains cold, pulseless. Ongoing monitoring.

author: Radiologist
note_text:
Findings:
- acute occlusion R femoral artery
- no significant underlying plaque

Impression: embolic arterial occlusion.

author: Vascular Surgeon
note_text:
Acute limb ischemia (Rutherford IIa–IIb), embolic likely secondary to AF.
Plan: urgent surgical embolectomy.
Risks discussed incl limb loss, bleeding, procedural complications. Consent obtained.

author: Vascular Surgeon
note_text:
R femoral artery exposed. Fogarty catheter passed proximally + distally.
Fresh embolus retrieved.
Immediate restoration of distal flow. Pulses palpable at end of procedure.
No intraop complications.

author: ICU Physician
note_text:
Pt stable.

R limb:
- warm
- normal coloration
- pulses palpable

No evidence compartment syndrome.
Plan:
- continue anticoagulation
- monitor perfusion
- analgesia

author: ICU Nurse
note_text:
Stable overnight.
Limb well perfused, warm. Pain reduced (~3/10).
No swelling, no concerns. Monitoring ongoing.

author: Cardiologist
note_text:
Event consistent w/ embolism secondary to AF without adequate anticoagulation.
Plan:
- initiate DOAC
- optimize rate control
- counsel re stroke/embolism risk

author: Vascular Surgery Team
note_text:
Recovering well.
Ambulating w/ assistance. Limb perfusion normal. No neuro deficit.
Plan: continue rehab + anticoagulation.

author: Physiotherapist
note_text:
Mobilizing w/ assistance.
Mild residual weakness R leg improving. Gait training initiated.

author: Ward Nurse
note_text:
Pt comfortable.
Ambulating short distances independently. No pain at rest. Independent w/ ADLs.
